## Getting the U.S. Census Bureau’s American Community Survey Data

```{r}
acs <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  state = "MA",
  year = 2024,
  survey = "acs5",
  variables = c(
    rent_burden_total = "B25070_001",
    rent_30_to_34 = "B25070_007",
    rent_35_to_39 = "B25070_008",
    rent_40_to_49 = "B25070_009",
    rent_50_plus = "B25070_010",
    burden_unknown = "B25070_011",
    renter_households = "B25003_003",
    median_gross_rent = "B25064_001",
    median_renter_income = "B25119_003"
  ),
  output = "wide"
)

# Count households spending 30% or more on rent and utilities.
burdened <- acs$rent_30_to_34E + acs$rent_35_to_39E +
  acs$rent_40_to_49E + acs$rent_50_plusE

# Use only households whose rent burden could be calculated.
known <- acs$rent_burden_totalE - acs$burden_unknownE
acs$pct_rent_burdened <- ifelse(known > 0, 100 * burdened / known, NA_real_)

dir.create("data", showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(acs, "data/acs_ma_tracts_2024.csv", row.names = FALSE)

head(acs[c("GEOID", "renter_householdsE", "pct_rent_burdened")])
```

## Getting the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development Data

```{r}
# Read HUD data as text so geographic IDs keep any leading zeros.
hud <- read.csv("data/hud_lihtc_properties.csv", colClasses = "character")

# Properties placed in service in 1997–2001 reach Year 30 in 2027–2031.
hud_ma <- subset(
  hud,
  PROJ_ST == "MA" & YR_PIS %in% as.character(1997:2001)
)

nrow(hud_ma)
table(hud_ma$YR_PIS)

# Find the tract-related columns available in this download.
grep("TRACT|GEOID", names(hud), value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(tigris)

# Keep records with usable coordinates and HUD's recommended quality codes.
hud_ma$LAT <- as.numeric(hud_ma$LAT)
hud_ma$LON <- as.numeric(hud_ma$LON)

hud_located <- subset(
  hud_ma,
  LVL2KX %in% c("R", "4") & is.finite(LAT) & is.finite(LON)
)

# Convert property coordinates to points and load 2024 tract boundaries.
properties <- st_as_sf(hud_located, coords = c("LON", "LAT"), crs = 4326)
ma_tracts <- tracts(state = "MA", year = 2024, cb = FALSE)
properties <- st_transform(properties, st_crs(ma_tracts))

# Assign a GEOID where the property matches exactly one tract.
matches <- st_intersects(properties, ma_tracts)
one_match <- lengths(matches) == 1

hud_located$GEOID <- NA_character_
hud_located$GEOID[one_match] <- ma_tracts$GEOID[
  unlist(matches[one_match], use.names = FALSE)
]

c(
  total_records = nrow(hud_ma),
  usable_coordinates = nrow(hud_located),
  matched_to_one_tract = sum(one_match)
)

head(hud_located[c("HUD_ID", "YR_PIS", "LI_UNITS", "GEOID")])
```

```{r}
# Keep the HUD records that matched a Census tract.
hud_matched <- subset(hud_located, !is.na(GEOID))
hud_matched$low_income_units <- as.numeric(hud_matched$LI_UNITS)

# Check for missing or negative unit counts and repeated HUD IDs.
c(
  tracts = length(unique(hud_matched$GEOID)),
  missing_unit_counts = sum(is.na(hud_matched$low_income_units)),
  negative_unit_counts = sum(hud_matched$low_income_units < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  repeated_hud_ids = sum(duplicated(hud_matched$HUD_ID))
)

# Check whether different records share the same street address and city.
address <- toupper(trimws(hud_matched$PROJ_ADD))
city <- toupper(trimws(hud_matched$PROJ_CTY))
address_key <- paste(city, address)
repeat_address <- !is.na(address) & nzchar(address) &
  (duplicated(address_key) | duplicated(address_key, fromLast = TRUE))

hud_matched[repeat_address,
            c("HUD_ID", "PROJECT", "PROJ_ADD", "PROJ_CTY", "YR_PIS", "LI_UNITS")]
```

```{r}
hud_matched[is.na(hud_matched$low_income_units),
            c("HUD_ID", "PROJECT", "PROJ_CTY", "GEOID", "LI_UNITS")]

hud_matched[repeat_address,
            c("HUD_ID", "PROJECT", "PROJ_ADD", "PROJ_CTY", "YR_PIS", "LI_UNITS")]
```

```{r}
# Count HUD records and add up reported units by tract.
hud_by_tract <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    hud_records = rep(1L, nrow(hud_matched)),
    missing_unit_counts = as.integer(is.na(hud_matched$low_income_units)),
    reported_low_income_units = replace(
      hud_matched$low_income_units,
      is.na(hud_matched$low_income_units),
      0
    )
  ) ~ GEOID,
  data = hud_matched,
  FUN = sum
)

# Leave the unit total unknown if every record in the tract is missing a count.
all_counts_missing <- hud_by_tract$missing_unit_counts == hud_by_tract$hud_records
hud_by_tract$reported_low_income_units[all_counts_missing] <- NA_real_

nrow(hud_by_tract)
hud_by_tract[hud_by_tract$GEOID == "25027757500", ]
sum(repeat_address)
```

```{r}
# Read the Census file and keep the tract ID as text.
acs_tracts <- read.csv(
  "data/acs_ma_tracts_2024.csv",
  colClasses = c(GEOID = "character")
)

# Check that the Census file has one row per tract.
stopifnot(anyDuplicated(acs_tracts$GEOID) == 0)

# Keep all HUD tracts and attach the Census data.
housing_tracts <- merge(
  hud_by_tract,
  acs_tracts,
  by = "GEOID",
  all.x = TRUE
)

# Check how many HUD tracts matched a Census row.
matched <- housing_tracts$GEOID %in% acs_tracts$GEOID

c(
  hud_tracts = nrow(housing_tracts),
  matched_to_acs = sum(matched),
  unmatched_to_acs = sum(!matched)
)

head(housing_tracts[c(
  "GEOID", "reported_low_income_units", "pct_rent_burdened"
)])
```

```{r}
# Keep tracts with values for both measures.
plot_data <- housing_tracts[complete.cases(
  housing_tracts[c("pct_rent_burdened", "reported_low_income_units")]
), ]

ggplot(plot_data, aes(
  x = pct_rent_burdened,
  y = reported_low_income_units
)) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Rent burden and low-income units approaching Year 30",
    subtitle = "Each point is a Massachusetts census tract",
    x = "Renters spending at least 30% of income on housing (%)",
    y = "Reported low-income units reaching Year 30, 2027–2031",
    caption = "Sources: HUD LIHTC property data and 2020–2024 ACS estimates"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Check how many merged tracts are shown in the plot.
c(plotted = nrow(plot_data), omitted = nrow(housing_tracts) - nrow(plot_data))
```

```{r}
tract_details <- plot_data[c(
  "GEOID", "NAME", "reported_low_income_units", "pct_rent_burdened"
)]

tract_details$pct_rent_burdened <- round(tract_details$pct_rent_burdened, 1)

head(tract_details[order(-tract_details$reported_low_income_units), ], 6)

c(plotted = nrow(plot_data), omitted = nrow(housing_tracts) - nrow(plot_data))
```
